run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The application is up (19/19 hotel-reservation pods Running and ready with 0 restarts, no OOM/eviction/failure events), but the /hotels read path is failing: frontend returns HTTP 500 on 'HTTP GET /hotels' because its child call to search fails, and search's calls to rate fail with DeadlineExceeded/ResourceExhausted. The fault originates in the rate service (Deployment rate): its own server spans for /rate.Rate/GetRates take ~12.77-12.79 s while its only downstream call (memcached_get_multi_rate) completes in ~0.43 ms, and 74% of its GetRates spans exceed 10 s (1146 of 1543.5). In the last sampled minute rate served ~1132 GetRates and returned 817 ERROR spans that are sub-millisecond and never reached memcached - i.e. admission-control rejections, not backend failures. The rate Deployment runs with RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT=20 and RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY=256, and the observed wait (12.78 s) matches capacity/token-rate (256/20) almost exactly, so the rate service is saturating its own admission queue at ~20 req/s while ~32.5 GetRates/s are offered; search's RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS=750 / RATE_RPC_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3 retry policy multiplies the offered load (2470 rate calls per 1057 frontend requests) and keeps the queue full. rate was fast in the first sampled minute (mean GetRates 0.400 ms, no ERROR spans) and degraded in the next (mean 5172 ms), so the throttling behaviour is recent and ongoing. The conclusion is partial: no pre-17:52 baseline exists and change history is not integrated, so I cannot show when/whether the rate limits were changed, and the initial trigger of the retry amplification is not established.

frontend spans for operation "HTTP GET /hotels" carry status tags error=true, http.status_code=500, otel.status_code=ERROR with durations between ~1.64 s and ~2.43 s; their child frontend span "/search.Search/Nearby" is also error=true, and the corresponding search server span "/search.Search/Nearby" is error=true at ~2.39 s.
search's client spans "/rate.Rate/GetRates" are error=true with durations of exactly ~750 ms (e.g. 750167 us, 751098 us, 750029 us), matching search's configured 750 ms RPC deadline.

rate's own server spans "/rate.Rate/GetRates" in the sampled traces are dominated by durations of 12773829-12789090 us (~12.78 s, status not_recorded), alongside a separate set of rate spans of 17-23 us and 400-1613 us that carry otel.status_code=ERROR.

Mean span duration per service/operation over the window: rate "/rate.Rate/GetRates" 8339.87 ms while rate's own outbound spans are memcached_get_multi_rate 0.430 ms and mongo_rate NaN (no measurable increase); geo 0.035 ms, profile 0.549 ms, reservation 0.591 ms, search "/search.Search/Nearby" 146.0 ms, frontend "HTTP GET /hotels" 161.5 ms.

rate "/rate.Rate/GetRates" duration histogram over the window is cumulative: le="10000" = 397.456 and le="+Inf" = 1543.501, i.e. ~1146 of 1543 GetRates spans (>74%) took longer than 10 s; le="1000" = 106.816.

Per-span-name increases over the window for service rate: /rate.Rate/GetRates 1543.50, memcached_get_multi_rate 1543.50, mongo_rate 0 - i.e. exactly one memcached lookup per recorded GetRates span and no MongoDB calls from rate.

rate counters between 17:53:25Z and 17:54:25Z: /rate.Rate/GetRates status STATUS_CODE_UNSET 279 -> 1411 (+1132), /rate.Rate/GetRates status STATUS_CODE_ERROR 0 -> 817, memcached_get_multi_rate 279 -> 1411 (+1132), mongo_rate 5 -> 5 (no increase). Error spans therefore appeared only in the last minute and the 817 errored GetRates produced no memcached span.

rate "/rate.Rate/GetRates" mean duration was 0.400 ms at 2026-11-21T17:53:25Z and 5172.25 ms at 2026-11-21T17:54:25Z, while its memcached_get_multi_rate mean stayed 0.295 ms -> 0.427 ms; rate degraded sharply inside that minute.

In the same minute (counters at 17:53:25Z vs 17:54:25Z) frontend "HTTP GET /hotels" went 281 -> 1057 (+776) and frontend "/search.Search/Nearby" 281 -> 1057, but search's client "/rate.Rate/GetRates" went 280 -> 2470 (+2190) and rate's server "/rate.Rate/GetRates" went 279 -> 2228 (+1949): the rate service received about 2.5 times more calls than frontend requests in that minute.

search pod search-7769dfc66b-pz524 repeatedly logs WRN services/search/server.go:252 "downstream request failed dependency=rate grpc_code=DeadlineExceeded" and the same line with "grpc_code=ResourceExhausted" between 17:54:17Z and 17:54:24Z (exact messages, dependency=rate).

count_over_time({namespace="hotel-reservation",app="search"} |= "downstream request failed" [1m]) rose from 17 lines at 17:53:22Z to 70 at 17:53:23Z and 358 at 17:53:30Z, so rate-failure log lines were already ramping in the minute before 17:54.

Deployment rate in namespace hotel-reservation sets exactly these env vars besides JAEGER_SAMPLE_RATIO=1: RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT=20 and RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY=256 (image ghcr.io/sregym/hotel-reservation@sha256:1c685e1c...).

Deployment search in namespace hotel-reservation sets RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS=750, RATE_RPC_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3, RATE_RPC_INITIAL_BACKOFF_MS=50, RATE_RPC_BACKOFF_MULTIPLIER=2.0, RATE_RPC_JITTER=0.2 (plus JAEGER_SAMPLE_RATIO=1).

A sweep of the env vars of all 19 deployments in hotel-reservation shows no latency/fault/failure/kill switch setting anywhere: besides JAEGER_SAMPLE_RATIO=1 the only settings are rate's two rate-limiting vars, search's five RATE_RPC_* vars, and memcached MEMCACHED_CACHE_SIZE/MEMCACHED_THREADS sizing; frontend, geo, profile, reservation, recommendation, user and the mongo deployments carry no extra settings.

frontend wrote stderr lines at 2026-11-21T17:52:25Z: "grpc/lb/consul: error retrieving instances from Consul ... dial tcp 10.96.229.179:8500: connect: connection refused" for srv-search, srv-profile and srv-recommendation, i.e. during the 17:52 startup while consul was not yet reachable.

rate is saturated at its own admission control, not at a dependency: the observed maximum GetRates wait of ~12.78 s equals RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY / RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT = 256/20 = 12.8 s, successful GetRates in the last minute ran at ~1132/60 ≈ 18.9/s (near the 20/s limit) while ~1949 GetRates/60 s ≈ 32.5/s were offered, and the 817 excess requests were rejected in 17-23 us without ever issuing a memcached call (yielding the ResourceExhausted grpc code seen in search's logs).

search's retry policy (RATE_RPC_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3 at RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS=750 with 50 ms initial backoff x2.0) is an amplifying, arguably co-configured, factor: 2.5 rate calls per frontend request pushed offered load above rate's 20/s ceiling and kept the queue full, and 3 x 750 ms + 150 ms backoff = 2.4 s matches the duration of the frontend 500s.

The degradation started around 17:53:2x-17:53:30Z, when rate was still fast (mean GetRates 0.400 ms, zero ERROR spans, 279 requests served) and search's rate-failure log count jumped from 17 to 358 per trailing minute; a momentary overload at the load ramp, amplified by the 3-attempt retry, could have seeded the backlog, but the initial trigger is not visible in the available data.

rate's dependencies are not the bottleneck: memcached_get_multi_rate averaged 0.427 ms and was invoked exactly once per successful GetRates (1411 spans for 1411 successful GetRates), and mongo_rate shows no call increase in the incident minute (5 -> 5 spans, 0 increase over the window); memcached-rate and mongodb-rate pods are Running and ready with 0 restarts.

geo, profile and reservation were checked and show no latency problem: geo "/geo.Geo/Nearby" mean 0.0347 ms, profile "/profile.Profile/GetProfiles" 0.549 ms (memcached_get_profile 0.470 ms, mongo_profile 1 call), reservation "/reservation.Reservation/CheckAvailability" 0.591 ms; frontend's own profile and reservation child spans averaged 1.27 ms and 1.30 ms.

Pod-level failure (crash, OOMKilled, eviction, failed readiness of a long-running pod) as the cause is rejected: every hotel-reservation pod reports restartCount 0 with no termination state, and the grouped events contain only Created/Pulled/Scheduled/Started/ScalingReplicaSet/SuccessfulCreate for this namespace.

The frontend consul "connection refused" errors are not this fault: they are single-shot stderr lines at 17:52:25Z during application startup (same second the pods started, before consul registration) and all frontend traffic afterwards reached search, whose own spans show the failure on its rate dependency.

Treat the rate service's admission settings in Deployment rate as the capacity limit to fix first (raise RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT well above the ~30 req/s retried demand or remove the queue bottleneck), and separately reduce search's retry amplification (fewer attempts, capped jittered backoff, circuit breaker) so retries cannot push offered load past rate's ceiling; alert on ResourceExhausted from rate.

gaps: No data exists before ~2026-11-21T17:52:25Z: metric counters for the suite begin in that minute (a 5-minute increase at 17:54:25 equals the whole counter lifetime, and an instant query at 2026-11-21T06:00:00Z returned no samples), so there is no pre-incident baseline for rate latency and I cannot show that 20 QPS/256 queue differs from an earlier healthy value.

The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so it could not be established when or by whom the rate (RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT, RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY) or search (RATE_RPC_*) env values were set; the values above are the ones currently in effect.

The initial trigger of the retry amplification is unknown: the first good sample (17:53:25Z) shows rate at 0.400 ms mean with no ERROR spans, and the first degraded sample is only 60 s later; no metric or log covers the transition in between.

The rate service writes no per-request log lines (only startup lines at 17:52:25-17:52:34Z), so the ResourceExhausted rejections are inferred from its sub-millisecond ERROR spans and search's log text, not from rate's own log messages; a Loki query for rate lines matching error/warn/exhaust/queue/limit over 17:52-17:54 returned nothing (status no_data), which is not proof that none were written.

Whether the queue/limit values come from application defaults or from configuration outside the visible env vars could not be verified: only three ConfigMaps exist in hotel-reservation (kube-root-ca.crt, mongo-geo-script, mongo-rate-script) and none configures the rate service; Secrets are not readable.
next_steps: Compare the rate Deployment's RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT/RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY against the application's documented default via the deployment manifest history (change_history is not integrated here).
Re-check rate GetRates latency and ResourceExhausted/DeadlineExceeded counts after any adjustment, over a window that includes a pre-change baseline, to confirm the queue saturation explanation.
Verify whether the load generator's ramp (frontend /hotels rose from ~5.6 req/s to ~13 req/s) alone exceeds rate's configured ceiling once search retries are counted, and size rate accordingly.
